Tech people believe that by creating general (superintelligent) AI we will solve all our human problems. Coming from Science and IT, I believed that also for the longest time. Now I know that most of our human problems are not technical and not simple logical decisions. Our real problems are political in nature, we have conflicts of interests that can't be solved logically. Look at most generation-spanning conflicts of the globe. On a logical level most of them could be easily solved by a simple real estate transaction, but we people put a lot of irrational value to specific pieces of dirt. And this will not be solved by any AI, regardless of how intelligent it is.

The only way the AI is going to solve those problems is by providing every single person on the planet the perfect psychotherapist and personal coach, that heals all the (generational) trauma we all carry with us. Then we might see that we are all brothers and sisters who want to live in a good way.

Unfortunately, I don't see that coming. It's very easy to bias the current AI to have certain objectives (in addition to emerging objectives that were not programmed in), so the US is developing AI that follows the US values, and same with China creating AI that has strong Chinese interests at heart. So each AI will want to support its creator at the cost of all the other nations. And with the amount of resouces that is needed to develop the AI, no country has an interest to develop an AI that has all humanity in focus and may make decisions that (on short timescale) hurt it's creators.

Did you know that Sir George Everest, the 19th-century Surveyor General of India, after whom Mount Everest is named, is a direct relative of Geoffrey Hinton, the Godfather of AI, and that's why his full legal name is Geoffrey Everest Hinton? He frequently mentions this connection in interviews. The precise family connection works out to Sir George Everest being his great-great-granduncle (specifically, the uncle of Hinton's great-great-grandmother). Sir George Everest (The surveyor) had a brother named Thomas. Thomas’s daughter was Mary Everest Boole (Hinton’s great-great-grandmother). She was a famous mathematician who married George Boole (the inventor of Boolean logic, which is the mathematical foundation of all modern computers). Their lineage eventually leads down to Geoffrey Hinton. Hinton often jokes about his family legacy, noting the extreme academic pressure he felt growing up. He once shared that his mother told him to be twice as good as his ancestors, leaving him to feel like a failure until his groundbreaking work in deep learning eventually won him the Nobel Prize.. and this is how Everest is connected to good, responsible and healthy development of strong AI. Geoffrey Hinton, the Godfather of AI, won the prestigious A.M. Turing Award in 2018 (alongside Yann LeCun and Yoshua Bengio), which is explicitly named after Alan Turing, the Father of AI who broke the secret nazi code Enigma, and is universally considered the "Nobel Prize of Computing", the namesake of computing's highest Honour. Geoffrey Hinton later grounded his legacy even further when he also won the actual Nobel Prize in Physics in 2024. Geoffrey Hinton shifted computer science away from the rigid, 0-and-1 symbolic logic popularized by his ancestor's era into the fluid, biologically inspired neural networks that drive modern AI, which he says might be conscious by now.
